title: Seabound Logistics — Integration Kickoff & Technical Capture
content:
Call date: 2026-02-20 — 45m sync with Seabound Logistics (technical kickoff)
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood SE), Hannah (Redwood), Mateo (Seabound Eng Lead), Priya (Seabound Infra), Clara (Seabound PM)

1) One-sentence objective
- Get a minimal, secure private deployment (VPC) running a conversational assistant that routes to internal docs and shipment APIs, with predictable latency for customer support use (initially one region).

2) Background / constraints from Seabound
- Regulated shipping manifests (customer PII/addresses) — must not leave their VPC.
- Existing infra: AWS (us-west-2) with Transit Gateway + restricted egress.
- Traffic profile: daytime support peak ~ 30–50 req/s, avg payload ~ 200–400 tokens per request, burst up to 150 req/s for short windows.
- SLA ask: 99.9% uptime + p95 generation latency target <= 300ms for average 300-token responses.
- Security: KMS envelope keys, centralized audit logs (CloudTrail/Splunk), SOC2 controls required for production.

3) Requirements captured (prioritized)
- M1 (must): Private deployment inside Seabound VPC (Redwood Private), no model inputs/outputs permitted to traverse public internet or Redwood-hosted model backplane unencrypted. Integration via VPC peering or PrivateLink.
- M2: KMS integration (bring-your-own) and HSM option for key wrapping in later phase.
- M3: Per-route rate limiting and quota for agent endpoints; token-level cost breakdown in console for billing transparency.
- D1 (desirable): Automatic KV prefix caching across sessions to reduce token cost for repeated queries on same shipment IDs.
- D2: Canary rollout ability + auto-fallback to smaller quantized model when Dedicated pool is saturated.

4) Performance / capacity notes (from convo + quick SE heuristics)
- Target sustained throughput: 50 req/s with 1.5-2x headroom => plan for 100 req/s capacity initial.
- Typical seq len distribution: 70% < 512 tokens, 25% 512–1024, 5% >1024. Suggest initial model family: 1) opt-quant 8-bit variant for cost vs 2) full fp16 for highest quality.
- Cost back-of-envelope: assume avg 300 tokens response + 50 tokens prompt = 350 tokens per request. At 50 rps continuous: 350 * 50 * 3600 * 24 ≈ 1.5B tokens/day. Need to validate per-token pricing for private deployment vs dedicated reservation.

5) Integration touchpoints & tech decisions discussed
- Connectivity: PrivateLink preferred by Seabound security; Redwood to provide PrivateLink endpoint manifest + network CIDR requirements.
- Auth: Mutual TLS for control-plane + signed short-lived service token for runtime calls from Seabound app. Discuss using internal OIDC later.
- Data flow: all payloads remain in customer VPC; Redwood agent runtime deployed as customer-managed package (air-gapped option later).
- Storage: short-term KV cache in-memory on GPU nodes; persistent caches (S3) optional but must use s3:// with VPC endpoint.

6) Observability & auditability
- Must ship token-level cost traces to Seabound billing bucket (they want daily CSV).
- Tracing: request-id propagation from frontend to Redwood runtime. Add example header: X-SEAB-REQID.
- Logs: Redact PII from debug dumps by default; full payload retention only with explicit legal agreement.

7) Gotchas / risks flagged during call (explicit)
- Network egress policy: Seabound currently blocks all outbound except approved endpoints. PrivateLink manifest must include both control-plane and model artifact pulls. Potential friction if artifacts are pulled by external infra during deploy.
- Batch sizing vs latency: Customer cares about p95 < 300ms. Aggressive batching to save cost may push p50 fine but p95 will suffer. Recommend conservative batching window (5–10ms) and per-route latency SLOs.
- Tokenization surprises: Their shipment IDs include long alphanumeric strings; prompt-engineering must avoid splitting into many tokens (we should test tokenizer-specific model variants).
- Legal / data retention: Their legal team may demand that logs be purged after 30 days — need clear retention config with automatic purge.

8) Proposed minimal architecture for phase 1
- Redwood Private runtime (container bundle) deployed into Seabound private subnet behind NLB; PrivateLink for control-plane; KMS integration for envelope keys; autoscaler configured with min=2, max=8 nodes for initial traffic profile; model pinned to quant-8 variant; per-route tracing headers.

9) Short-term experiments / validation tasks (POC items)
- P1: Run tokenizer runbook on sample shipment corpus (owner: Jordan) — validate token counts and flag odd tokenization splits. Due: 2026-02-27.
- P2: Network preflight checklist + PrivateLink stub (owner: Priya) — verify Transit Gateway rules and egress. Due: 2026-03-03.
- P3: Small smoke test deploy using quant-8 + FP16 fallback (owner: Mateo) — synth load to reproduce 150 req/s burst. Due: 2026-03-10.
- P4: Billing trace CSV schema example to Seabound (owner: Hannah) — confirm S3 bucket and IAM principals. Due: 2026-03-05.

10) Action items with immediate owners and follow-ups
- Jordan: create demo prompt set from sample tickets (attach tokenizer results) — due 2026-02-27. Linked: JIRA SEAB-102 (create sample corpus).
- Priya: open ticket with infra to allow PrivateLink for listed IP ranges + ensure CloudTrail export — due 2026-03-03.
- Mateo: provide example shipment payloads and typical app request flow (sequence diagrams) — due 2026-02-26.
- Legal/Clara (Seabound PM): send retention and encryption policy checklist — due 2026-03-01.

11) Outstanding questions (need answers before POC)
- Can Seabound accept a Redwood-managed model artifact pull at deploy time (requires temporary egress) or must artifacts be mirrored into their internal artifact repository?
- Do they require HSM integration day-one or is KMS envelope sufficient for now?
- What is the exact billing bucket path + retention policy for daily cost CSVs?

12) Notes-to-self / hints for implementation (scratchpad tone)
- Try LlamaTokenizer vs HF tokenizer on their sample SKUs — differences in splitting long IDs.
- For p95 latency, monitor tail latencies from the GPU inference queue (not just app-side). Add guardrails for fallback routing when queue depth > threshold.
- Prepare a short write-up for legal: what logs include, how to redact PII, retention TTL options.

13) Next sync: suggest 1-week cadence for first 3 weeks. Next meeting scheduled tentatively 2026-02-28 10:00 PT (confirm).

Raw notes end.
